title: Ronaldo Scores His First World Cup Knockout Goal. Then Ramos Wins It in Stoppage Time. Portugal Edge Croatia in Toronto.
excerpt: Cristiano Ronaldo equalised from the penalty spot, Gonçalo Ramos headed a 90th-minute winner, and a VAR-disallowed Croatian equaliser completed the chaos at BMO Field. Spain await in the round of 16.
body:
For 53 minutes, this match followed a familiar World Cup script: two European heavyweights probing, waiting for someone to blink. Then Ivan Perišić gave Croatia the lead, Cristiano Ronaldo answered from the penalty spot, Gonçalo Ramos rose for a stoppage-time header — and BMO Field in Toronto erupted, collapsed, and erupted again in the space of twenty minutes.

Portugal beat Croatia 2-1 in the round of 32, advancing to face Spain in what promises to be one of the defining fixtures of the 2026 World Cup. But the scoreline barely captures the drama of a second half that refused to end.

Perišić Strikes First

The first half in Toronto was cautious, shaped by tactical discipline on both sides. Portugal dominated possession without creating clear-cut chances, while Croatia looked to counter through the ageing but still dangerous Luka Modrić. Rúben Dias picked up an early yellow card, and the half ended goalless.

The second half brought chaos almost immediately. In the 53rd minute, Josip Stanišić played a cross into the box and Perišić, timing his run perfectly, got ahead of his marker and steered the ball past the Portuguese goalkeeper. Croatia 1, Portugal 0. BMO Field's sizeable Croatian contingent roared.

Ronaldo Finally Gets His Knockout Goal

For all Cristiano Ronaldo has achieved — five Ballons d'Or, Champions League titles, over 900 career goals — a World Cup knockout-round goal had somehow eluded him. In five previous World Cups, he had never scored once the tournament entered its elimination phase.

> "BMO Field's sizeable Croatian contingent roared."

That changed in the 68th minute. After a VAR review confirmed a handball by Nikola Vlašić in the box, Ronaldo stepped up and converted the penalty. One-all. At 41, he had finally written a line that was missing from his résumé.

Roberto Martínez then made a decision that drew audible surprise from the stadium. With nine minutes of normal time remaining, he substituted Ronaldo off, replacing him with Rúben Neves. Ronaldo shook his manager's hand, then shook his head. He walked to the bench knowing he had done his part.

Ramos Rises in the 94th Minute

![World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg)

With ten minutes of stoppage time announced, both sides traded chances. Croatia's Mario Pašalić headed just wide from a superb Petar Sučić cross. The match looked destined for extra time.

Then, in the 94th minute, Rafael Leão floated a cross from the left. Gonçalo Ramos, who had come on as a substitute, rose between two Croatian defenders and guided a textbook header past Dominik Livaković. Portugal 2, Croatia 1. Ronaldo sprinted off the bench to embrace Ramos.

The Goal That Wasn't

Croatia were not finished. In the 103rd minute — thirteen minutes into stoppage time — Joško Gvardiol bundled the ball into the net from close range. BMO Field exploded. The Croatian bench poured onto the pitch.

Then the referee signalled for a VAR review. The check revealed that Pašalić, who had laid the ball across for Gvardiol, was in an offside position when the ball had taken a deflection. The goal was disallowed. Croatia's World Cup was over.

Modrić, 40, sank to his knees. This was almost certainly his last World Cup match — a career that included a runner-up finish in 2018 and a semifinal in 2022, ending in the round of 32 in Toronto.

What It Means for NRIs in Canada

Toronto is home to one of the largest Indian diaspora communities in the world, with over 700,000 people of South Asian origin in the Greater Toronto Area. BMO Field's 43,000-seat capacity was full for the occasion, and the city's diverse fan base meant the stadium held pockets of support for every flag.

For the NRIs who secured tickets, the drama was worth every dollar. Toronto has hosted some of the tournament's most memorable matches, and this one joins the list.

Spain Await

Portugal's reward is a round-of-16 clash against Spain on Monday, July 6, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. Spain demolished Austria 3-0 earlier in the day at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring twice and Pedro Porro heading in between. The European champions have not conceded a goal in the tournament.

An Iberian derby in the World Cup knockout rounds — with Ronaldo's farewell narrative running in parallel — is the kind of fixture the tournament was built for. For NRIs in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, it may be the hottest ticket of the summer.
